---
title: "Content Author Guide"
---

This chapter tells a content author what to know to work in this repository. Part 1 gives the
overview, the setup and the workflow. Part 2 is about the book's chapter notebooks. Part 3, the
largest part, is about the **Prof. Rosenthal's Review** pages.

## Part 1: the repository

### What the repository holds

The repository is a fork of Allen Downey's *Think Python*, 3rd edition. The course adds its own
material, and keeps it apart from the book.

| Folder or file | What it holds | Do you edit it? |
|---|---|---|
| `chapters/chapNN.ipynb` | The book's chapters, 0 to 19 | Yes, carefully (Part 2) |
| `blank/chapNN.ipynb` | "Fill in the blanks" copies of the chapters | No: a tool writes them |
| `solutions/chapNN.ipynb` | Suggested solutions to the book's exercises | Yes (Part 2) |
| `yr/chapNN_review.ipynb` | The review pages, one per chapter (2 to 7 so far) | Yes (Part 3) |
| `yr/README.md` | The rules for the review pages | Yes, when a rule changes |
| `yr/tools/` | The review-page tools | Only to change a tool |
| `jb/` | The website build (Jupyter Book) | Rarely |
| `.claude/skills/` | Instructions that Claude Code follows | When a rule changes |
| `author-guide/` | This guide (a Quarto book) | Yes |

The website is <https://y-rosenthal.github.io/yrThinkPython/>. Each review page shows on the
website right after its chapter, as "4b. Prof. Rosenthal's Review" (for chapter 4). Each page also
has a "Run this page on Colab" link.

### Set up your computer

You need Linux or macOS, `git`, and Python 3.12 at `/usr/bin/python3`. The tools create the rest:

- **The book's venv**, `~/.venvs/yrThinkPython`. The build scripts create it the first time.
  The repository is in Dropbox, so the venv is outside it.
- **The Colab-like kernel**, `~/.venvs/colablike`. `yr/tools/review.sh` creates it the first
  time you run `sync` or `check`. It has the same Python, IPython and ipykernel versions as Colab
  (Python 3.13, IPython 7.34.0, ipykernel 6.17.1). The tools write the stored outputs of the
  review pages with this kernel only, so the pages look the same as in Colab.
- **`uv`**, the tool that builds the Colab-like kernel. `review.sh` installs it into the book's
  venv if it is missing.

Run all commands from the root folder of the repository.

### The workflow: branch, check, publish

Every push to the branch `v3` publishes the website. Thus:

1. Make a topic branch before you change anything:

   ```bash
   git switch v3
   git pull
   git switch -c my-topic
   ```

2. Make your changes, and run the checks for what you changed (the next chapters tell you which).
3. Always run the fast check of all notebooks:

   ```bash
   python3 .claude/skills/check-notebooks/check_notebooks.py
   ```

4. Build the website on your computer, and look at the pages you changed:

   ```bash
   .claude/skills/build-book/build_book.sh
   ```

   The output is in `jb/_build/html/`. The script must say "no new warnings".
5. Commit, and push your branch.
6. To publish, merge the branch into `v3` and push `v3`. The `yrpublish` skill of Claude Code does
   all the checks, the merge, the push and a check of the live site.

The deploy workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-book.yml`) runs `check_notebooks.py` first. If it
finds a problem, the website does not change.

**Corrections to the book itself** go to Allen Downey as a GitHub issue, not as a pull request.
The `contribute-upstream` skill writes the issue text.

## Part 2: the chapter notebooks

The book's chapters are in `chapters/`. The website shows them, and Colab opens them. Keep your
changes small, because the fork must stay close to Downey's version.

- **Find a cell** before you change it:

  ```bash
  python3 .claude/skills/notebook-conventions/nb_cells.py chapters/chap03.ipynb
  ```

- **Do not store outputs.** The website build runs the chapters and makes the outputs.
- **Tag your additions.** Give each cell that you add or change for the course the tag `course`.
  Do not tag a correction of an error in the book.
- **Exercises** have code cells that contain only `# Solution goes here`. Put a suggested solution
  in `solutions/chapNN.ipynb`, in the cell with the same id. The website shows it in a closed
  "Suggested solution" box.
- **Expected errors** use the cell magic `%%expect ErrorName` on the first line.
- **After a change**, run the checks, and run the changed chapter:

  ```bash
  python3 .claude/skills/check-notebooks/check_notebooks.py
  .claude/skills/check-notebooks/run_notebooks.sh chapters/chap03.ipynb
  ```

- **Blank versions.** If the chapter has a `blank/` copy, make it again with the `make-blank`
  skill.

New course material does not go in `chapters/`. It goes in a review page (Part 3).

## Part 3: the review pages

### What a review page is

A review page (`yr/chapNN_review.ipynb`) helps students review one chapter. It has:

1. **Concepts covered**: two lists of facts, as a checklist.
2. **Questions**: practice questions, from easy to hard. Each question has an **Answer** that is
   closed until the student opens it.

### What a student sees

In Colab:

- Each Answer is closed. The student clicks the arrow next to **Answer** to open it.
- An Answer can show the real output of the question's code (printed text, an error, a drawing).
  The output is stored in the page, so the student sees it before running anything.
- The student can use **Runtime → Run all**. Run all runs the whole page, and it does not stop at
  the questions whose answer is an error. All Answers stay closed.
- The question's code is text, not a code cell. Thus, Colab's editor does not mark the mistakes in
  the code before the student makes a prediction.
- After Run all, the student can copy any code block from an Answer into a new cell, and run it.

On the website, each Answer is a closed box with the explanation and the stored outputs.

### The main rule: type each fact once

You type each fact one time. The tools write the rest by running the code.

| You type | The tools write |
|---|---|
| The question's code | The hidden cell that runs it, and its output |
| The explanation, with a marker for each error name | The error name |
| Each helper function, in one cell | "Run this cell to define ..." and "This question uses ... from Question N" |
| The task and the example calls | The "Start from this header" block, and the output of each example |
| The solutions (no imports, no example calls) | The import lines of each solution, and a "Then try:" line |
| Fixes and "what if" code | Their outputs and pictures |
| Each value in the text, as an expression | The value |

Two commands do the work:

- `yr/tools/review.sh sync PAGE` writes everything in the right column.
- `yr/tools/review.sh check PAGE` makes sure that the page is correct. It fails if `sync` would
  change something, so it also finds text that somebody typed in a place that the tools write.

### The steps to add a question

1. **Get the question number.** Numbers stay the same during a semester, because homework uses
   them. A question between Questions 3 and 4 is Question 3b:

   ```bash
   python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py next yr/chap05_review.ipynb --before 4
   ```

   For a question at the end of the page, do not use `--before`.

2. **Write the question in a spec file.** A spec file is a text file of cells. Each cell starts
   with a line `%%% KIND`. Section "Each kind of question" shows examples. These are the kinds:

   | Line | The cell it makes |
   |---|---|
   | `%%% markdown` | A text cell: the heading, the task, examples |
   | `%%% run` or `%%% run a` | The question's code (a "run block"); `a`, `b`, ... for parts |
   | `%%% code` | A definition cell: a helper that the question gives (definitions only) |
   | `%%% placeholder` | A `# Your code here` cell for the student |
   | `%%% placeholder no-signature` | The same, for a task without a function |
   | `%%% answer` | The `#### Answer` heading; text after it goes into the first Answer cell |
   | `%%% part a` | An Answer cell that explains part a |

3. **Add the cells to the page:**

   ```bash
   python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py add yr/chap05_review.ipynb my-question.txt --before 4
   ```

   You can also edit the notebook in Jupyter. Do not edit it in Colab (see "If you edit a page in
   Colab").

4. **Run sync:**

   ```bash
   yr/tools/review.sh sync yr/chap05_review.ipynb
   ```

   Read the report. It shows each new output and each new value. Make sure that your text agrees
   with them. Section "Read the report of sync" tells you what to do with each message.

5. **Run check:**

   ```bash
   yr/tools/review.sh check yr/chap05_review.ipynb
   ```

   It must print `OK`. If it shows problems, correct the question and do steps 4 and 5 again.

6. **Run the notebook check and the website build** (Part 1, steps 3 and 4). Look at the page.

### Each kind of question

#### What is displayed, drawn, or what happens

Type the code in a run block. In the Answer, write each value as an expression, then the marker
`<!--=-->`, then `` `?` ``. Sync puts the value in place of the `?`.

```text
%%% markdown
### Question 3b (easy): what is displayed?

Predict what this code displays, then open the Answer to check.
%%% run
minutes = 135
print(minutes // 60, minutes % 60)
%%% answer
135 minutes is 2 hours (`135 // 60` is <!--=-->`?`) and `135 % 60` is <!--=-->`?` minutes left over.
```

Sync adds a hidden cell under the Answer heading. This cell shows the real output of the code.

#### Find the error, in parts

Use one run block for each part (`%%% run a`, `%%% run b`) and one Answer cell for each part
(`%%% part a`). Write `` <!--=error-->`?` `` where the text names the error. Sync writes the name of
the error that the part's code really gives.

```text
%%% markdown
### Question 9 (medium): find the error

Each part has one mistake. Predict the error for each, then open the Answer to check.
%%% run a
x = 5
if x = 5:
    print('five')
%%% run b
print(undefined_name)
%%% answer
%%% part a
`=` assigns; comparing needs `==`, so this is a <!--=error-->`?`.
%%% part b
The name was never assigned: a <!--=error-->`?`.
%%% markdown
Python finds a syntax error before it runs any of that part's code.
```

The last markdown cell is the summary. Sync puts the output of each part after the explanation of
that part. The output shows the traceback as text, so Run all does not stop and Colab shows no red
marks.

#### Write a function

Type the task, a line that starts with `**Examples**`, and the example calls in
```` ```python ```` blocks. Type the solution in the Answer. **Do not type:**

- the "Start from this header" block;
- the output of the examples;
- import lines in the solution;
- example calls in the solution.

````text
%%% markdown
### Question 10 (medium): write a function

Write a function called `end_hour` that takes `start` and `duration` and displays the hour
when the event ends, on a 24-hour clock.

**Examples**

```python
end_hour(9, 3)
end_hour(22, 5)
```

```python
end_hour(20, 28)
```
%%% placeholder
%%% answer
```python
def end_hour(start, duration):
    print((start + duration) % 24)
```
````

Each ```` ```python ```` block in this Answer is a solution. `check` runs each solution with each
example, and all must give the same output.

- A block that is not a full solution (for example, a first draft) gets the line
  `<!-- not a solution -->` immediately above it. Sync then writes the output of that block.
- If the solution has a helper function, the header shows it too. To show only some functions,
  write `<!-- header: end_hour -->` on its own line in the task.

#### Write code without a function

The student writes code that uses variables that already have values. Tag the student's cell
`no-signature`. Make the first example a definition cell, so that Run all gives values to the
variables. Sync writes the output of that example in the text cell after it.

````text
%%% markdown
### Question 11 (medium): write code

The variables `hours` and `minutes` have values. Write code that displays the total number of
minutes.

**Examples** (each example assigns the variables; your code comes after them)
%%% code
hours = 1
minutes = 2
%%% markdown
```python
hours = 0
minutes = 42
```
%%% placeholder no-signature
%%% answer
```python
print(hours * 60 + minutes)
```
````

The solution contains only the computation, not the example values.

#### A question that gives a helper function

Put the helper in a definition cell (`%%% code`). Give each helper only one time, in the first
question that uses it. Sync writes "Run this cell to define `square`." above the cell. A later
question that uses the helper gets the line "This question uses `square` from Question 11."

A definition cell can contain only definitions: `def`, `class`, `import` and assignments. It must
display nothing.

#### Wrong calls (predict the error)

First show two correct calls in ```` ```python ```` blocks in the task. Sync writes their outputs.
Then give the wrong calls as run blocks, in parts.

#### Fixes and "what if" code in an Answer

Write a short ```` ```python ```` block in the Answer. Sync runs it after the question's code and
writes its output or picture under it.

- **Only the changed lines.** For example, `average = (score1 + score2 + score3) / 3` and
  `print(average)`.
- **Only the new `def`.** Sync then runs the question's own calls after it.
- **Keep an input line** if a later question gives the same name a new value. After Run all, the
  name has the later value. `check` prints a note with the names that more than one question
  assigns.
- **The full code with one change.** Write a `derive` marker on its own line, and an empty block
  under it. Sync fills the block:

  ````text
  <!-- derive: from=Q14 replace="for letter in word:" with="for letter in word.lower():" -->
  ```python
  ```
  ````

  `from=Q14` uses Question 14's run block. If the text to replace is in Question 14's definition
  cell, sync uses the definition cell and the run block. `from=solution` uses the first solution
  of this question. In OLD and NEW, `\n` is a line break.

#### Drawings (jupyturtle)

Start each drawing with `make_turtle()`. The canvas is 300 × 150. The turtle starts in the middle,
facing east. To make room, use `jump(-x)` or `make_turtle(width=..., height=...)`. Sync makes each
picture. Look at new pictures on the built page.

### Markers

Markers are HTML comments. Colab, Jupyter and GitHub do not show them. The website build removes
them. You type `?` as the value, and sync writes the value.

| You type | Sync writes |
|---|---|
| `` `EXPR` is <!--=-->`?` `` | The value of the code before the marker, on the same line |
| `` <!--= EXPR -->`?` `` | The value of EXPR. Statements before it are allowed: `<!--= import sys; sys.getrecursionlimit() -->` |
| `` <!--=error-->`?` `` | The error name that this part's code gives (in the summary: the error that all parts give) |
| `<!--do: CODE -->` | Nothing: CODE runs before the values after it, in the same cell |
| `<!-- not a solution -->` | The output of the next ```` ```python ```` block |
| `<!-- header: f g -->` | A header block for these functions only |
| `<!-- derive: from=QN replace="OLD" with="NEW" -->` | The next ```` ```python ```` block |

Two rules:

- **A value marker must not start a line or a list item.** If it does, Colab shows the line as raw
  HTML. Write "`` `-7 // 2` is <!--=-->`?` ``", not "`` <!--= -7 // 2 -->`?` is ... ``".
- **A block marker** (the last three rows) is alone on its line.

Sync shows each value as a notebook shows it: `'abc'` with quotes, `4.0`. In the Concepts lists,
sync computes values after the setup cell only. In a question, sync computes them after Run all and
after the question's code.

### What sync writes (do not edit it)

- **Run cells.** One hidden cell for each run block, with the title "Output of Question 8a" and
  the stored output. Code that gives an error, or prints a line number, calls the page's
  `run_code` helper. This helper prints the traceback as text.
- **Generated regions.** Text between `<!-- begin generated: KIND -->` and
  `<!-- end generated: KIND -->`. The kinds are `header`, `example`, `output`, `then-try`, `uses`
  and `define`.
- **Import lines.** The line `<!-- generated imports: N -->` above a code block tells you that sync
  wrote the first N lines of the block.
- **Values** in place of each `?`.
- **Template cells.** The title cell, the help note "Using this page in Colab or Jupyter", the
  helper cell "Helper for the Answers", and the credits.
- **The stamp.** Notebook metadata `yr_review`: the versions that wrote the outputs, and
  checksums. `check` uses them to find changes that somebody made by hand.

### Read the report of sync

| Message | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `new ... output` or `value of ... is ...` | Sync wrote something new | Make sure that the text agrees with it |
| `NOT WRITTEN: these would change` | A stored output, region or value would change | Read the Answer again. If it is still correct, run `sync` again with `--accept` |
| `REFUSED, nothing written` | Sync cannot continue | Read the reasons, correct the page, run `sync` again |
| `the solutions disagree` | Two solutions give different outputs for an example | Correct a solution, or mark a draft `<!-- not a solution -->` |
| `the kernel ... runs ..., not the pinned Colab-like stack` | The wrong kernel | Run `yr/tools/ensure_colab_venv.sh`, or use `review.sh`, which does it |
| `derive marker: ... occurs N times` | The OLD text must occur exactly one time | Use a longer OLD text |
| `the expression has no value` | A value marker's expression displays nothing | Use an expression, not a statement |

### The format rules that check enforces

`check` gives each problem a rule number:

| Rule | The rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | Question headings are `### Question N (level): kind`; each N is unique on the page |
| 2 | Numbers do not change during a semester; a question "3b" must not exist while Question 3 has a part b |
| 3 | One `#### Answer` heading for each question, saved closed; no other headings in a question |
| 4 | Run blocks (`~~~python`) only before the Answer; with two or more, labels `**Part a**`, `**Part b**`, ... |
| 5 | Code cells before the Answer: definition cells and `# Your code here` only |
| 6 | Code cells in an Answer: run cells only |
| 7 | A ```` ```text ```` block or a picture appears only inside a generated region |
| 8 | Each error that a run cell gives has a `<!--=error-->` marker; the text of a part names no other error |
| 9 | Stored outputs only on run cells, as sync wrote them |
| 10 | Markers as in the table; no `?` left |
| 11 | Sync would change nothing |
| 12 | Each code block in an Answer imports what it uses, runs after Run all, and shows what the page says |
| 13 | A "NameError" answer stays true: no other cell assigns that name |
| 14 | The page ends with the credits; tags only `setup`, `no-signature`, and `remove-cell` (help note) |
| 16 | No `TODO` left; no `(c)`, `(r)`, `(tm)` or `+-` in the text (the website changes them to symbols) |

`check --static` runs only the rules that do not need a kernel. It is fast.

### Style rules

These rules come from Prof. Rosenthal. The full list is in `yr/README.md`, "Style rules".

**Concepts covered**

- Write a checklist of facts, as in an instruction manual. Give little or no explanation.
- Use plain English and little notation. Do not use arrows or symbols as short forms.
- Show the general form with UPPERCASE placeholders, say what it does in one sentence, then give an
  example.
- An example is not a fact. State the rule.
- **Python Syntax and Semantics** holds the facts about Python. **Definitions, etc.** holds the
  definitions (`DEFINITION: **term** is ...`), then **Other ideas**.

**Questions**

- Most questions are "what is displayed / drawn / happens" or "write code".
- Each question must make sense to a person who never read *Think Python*. Do not refer to the book.
- Give each helper that a question uses.
- Put the questions in order, from easy to hard. Put the level in the heading.
- Use only the Python that the chapter (or an earlier chapter) teaches, or explain the new part.
- Put the main point about Python first. Put other remarks last, in a paragraph that starts with
  "**By the way:**".
- For parts, write **Part a**, **Part b**. Do not write "(c)".

**Answers**

- Give more than one approach when there is more than one good approach.
- A student must be able to copy any code block of an Answer into a new cell after Run all, and run
  it.

### Change a question

1. Edit the cells that you typed (in Jupyter, or with a small `json` script). Keep the cell ids.
2. Do not edit the run cells, the generated regions, or the values.
3. Run `sync`, then `check`.

If you change a question's code, sync makes its run cell again. If the output changes, sync asks
you to read the Answer again (`NOT WRITTEN`). Use `--accept` only if the Answer is still correct.

### Question numbers between semesters

During a semester, do not change a number. Use letters for new questions (3b, 3c). At the start of
a new semester, you can number the questions 1, 2, 3, ... again:

```bash
python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py renumber yr/chap05_review.ipynb
yr/tools/review.sh sync yr/chap05_review.ipynb
```

`renumber` also changes "Question N" in the text, the `derive` markers and the run-cell titles.
Read the changed text before you commit.

### A new review page

Use the `yr-review-page` skill, or do these steps:

1. Make the page:

   ```bash
   python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py new 8 "Strings and Regular Expressions"
   ```

2. Write the two Concepts lists and the questions.
3. Add the page to `jb/_toc.yml`, after its chapter (see how `yr/chap04_review` is listed).
4. Add its Colab link to `jb/index.md`, under its chapter.
5. Run `sync`, `check`, the notebook check, and the website build.
6. Check the page on the built website:

   ```bash
   python3 yr/tools/verify_site.py jb/_build/html/yr/chap08_review.html yr/chap08_review.ipynb
   ```

### If you edit a page in Colab

Colab adds metadata and outputs when it saves a page. Do not save a page from Colab to GitHub. If
it happened, repair the page:

```bash
yr/tools/review.sh normalize yr/chap05_review.ipynb
yr/tools/review.sh sync yr/chap05_review.ipynb
```

### How the website shows a review page

The website build does not run the review pages. `jb/prep_notebooks.py` changes each page:

- Each Answer becomes one closed box, with the explanation and the stored outputs, without code.
- The markers go; the values stay.
- The help note, the helper cell, and the `# Your code here` cells go.
- Tracebacks are shorter.

## Tools reference

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py list PAGE` | Lists the questions |
| `python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py next PAGE [--before N]` | Prints the number for a new question |
| `python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py add PAGE SPEC [--before N]` | Adds the cells of a spec file |
| `python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py new NN "Title"` | Makes a new review page |
| `python3 yr/tools/review_cells.py renumber PAGE` | Numbers the questions again (between semesters only) |
| `yr/tools/review.sh sync PAGE [--accept]` | Writes all that can be derived, by running the code |
| `yr/tools/review.sh check PAGE [--static]` | Checks a page |
| `yr/tools/review.sh normalize PAGE` | Repairs a page that Colab saved |
| `yr/tools/review.sh selftest` | Tests the tools (run it after you change a tool) |
| `python3 yr/tools/verify_site.py HTML PAGE [BEFORE.html]` | Checks a page on the built website |
| `python3 .claude/skills/check-notebooks/check_notebooks.py` | Fast check of all notebooks |
| `.claude/skills/check-notebooks/run_notebooks.sh chapters/chapNN.ipynb` | Runs a chapter |
| `.claude/skills/build-book/build_book.sh` | Builds the website on your computer |
| `python3 .claude/skills/yrpublish/verify_live.py` | Checks the live website |

## Working with Claude Code

Claude Code follows the skills in `.claude/skills/`. You can ask in your own words, or type the
skill name:

| Skill | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `yr-review-questions` | Add, change or check questions on a review page |
| `yr-review-page` | Make a review page, or write its Concepts lists |
| `notebook-conventions` | Edit a chapter notebook |
| `make-blank` | Make the `blank/` copy of a chapter again |
| `check-notebooks` | Check or run notebooks |
| `build-book` | Build the website on your computer |
| `yrpublish` | Check, merge into `v3`, push, and check the live site |
| `sync-upstream` | Get the changes from Downey's repository |
| `upstream-diff` | See how the fork differs from Downey's version |
| `contribute-upstream` | Send a correction to Downey as a GitHub issue |

When a rule or a tool changes, change `yr/README.md`, the two review skills and this guide in the
same commit.

## Troubleshooting

- **`check` says rule 11 (sync would change the page).** Run `sync` and read its report.
- **`check` says rule 9 (stored outputs differ, or generated text was edited).** Somebody changed
  text that sync writes. Run `sync`, and read the differences before you use `--accept`.
- **`check` says rule 12 (an Answer block does not run).** The block uses a name that it does not
  import or define, or its output is not what the page says. Run `sync` (it writes the imports).
  If the problem stays, the block needs its own input line, or the solution is wrong.
- **`check` says rule 2 (a published number is gone).** You changed or removed a question number.
  Use its old number again, and give the new question a letter (3b).
- **A value marker shows as raw HTML in Colab.** The marker starts a line. Put some text before it.
- **The build stops with "prep_notebooks: ... Answer dropdowns".** A page has a problem. Run
  `check` on the page.
- **Colab says "Too many sessions".** End old sessions: **Connect ▾ → Manage sessions**.
